source_text: Quod igitur ad Hebraeos positum est: Ex uno omnes, exigit laus Dei, post commemorationem tamen parentum; quod autem dicitur de Christo: Qui sanctificat et sanctificantur ex uno omnes [n120] , ad Deum relatum est.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore has been placed to the Hebrews: From one all, the praise of God demands, after the commemoration nevertheless of the parents; but what is said of Christ: He who sanctifies and those sanctified all from one, has been referred to God.
pass_b_english: The phrase in Hebrews, ‘All from one,’ is required by the praise of God, after the parents have first been mentioned. But what is said about Christ—‘The one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one’ (Hebrews 2:11) (Hebrews 11:12)—refers to God.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: First clause returns to Abraham and his descendants.
From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
